headline: DE-DOLLARIZATION ALERT: MAJOR INTERNATIONAL BANK JOINS CHINA'S CIPS PAYMENT SYSTEM — BRICS Summit Backdrop; Gold Bid On Reserve Currency Erosion Thesis
snippet: A major international financial institution joined China's Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) on August 3, 2026, ahead of the September BRICS Summit — the latest step in the multi-year infrastructure buildout China is deploying to reduce global settlement dependence on SWIFT and the US dollar. Money Metals Exchange flags the development as a structural gold positive: each incremental CIPS adoption reduces the friction cost of central bank reserve diversification away from US Treasuries and into gold, reinforcing the demand-side floor under gold at $4,000–4,100 that analysts from Frank Holmes to John Paulson cite as the cycle's baseline. For junior mining investors, the de-dollarization trade is not a short-term catalyst but a structural re-rating mechanism — it is the reason central bank gold demand has exceeded 1,000 tonnes/year since 2022 and why the $3,900 support level has held through every macro headwind this year.

headline: GOLD SWOT AUG 3: GOLD MINING STOCKS TEEING UP FOR FURTHER GROWTH — Seasonal Autumn Rally Pattern Emerging; U.S. Global Investors Weekly Edition
snippet: US Global Investors' Frank Holmes published the August 3, 2026 Monday Gold SWOT report identifying gold mining stocks as positioned for the seasonal autumn rally, flagging strength in the August–September GDX accumulation window and noting that compressed gold equity valuations at current $4,067–4,100 spot represent an entry point consistent with prior mid-cycle corrections that preceded the next bull leg. The weekly SWOT format (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) highlights central bank demand and BRICS de-dollarization momentum as ongoing structural strengths, while real yield pressure and the 67% September Fed hike probability remain the primary threats. For TSX-V junior investors, the Holmes autumn rally framing is relevant because institutional capital that rotates into GDX-type seniors in August historically cascades into smaller-cap explorers with a 4–6 week lag, making the September–October window the key junior re-rating period.

headline: ZIJIN DROPS C$5.5B ALLIED GOLD TAKEOVER — Takes US$295M Strategic 9.2% Stake Instead; Chinese Regulatory Approval Failed; Closes ~Aug 10 (TSX: AAUC)
snippet: Zijin Mining's C$5.5 billion all-cash takeover of Allied Gold Corp (TSX: AAUC) collapsed on July 29, 2026 after failing to secure Chinese regulatory approval — with Zijin instead subscribing for a US$295 million strategic minority stake representing approximately 9.2% of Allied's shares at C$32.55 each, with the investment expected to close around August 10. The collapse ends what would have been the largest Chinese acquisition of a gold producer outside China since Zhaojin's 2024 Tietto deal, and leaves Allied Gold as an independent mid-tier producer with a significant but non-controlling Chinese strategic investor. For the sector, the deal failure reinforces the regulatory friction facing Chinese mining M&A in Western-listed gold companies — and raises the question of whether another strategic or industrial buyer emerges for Allied, or whether the 9.2% Zijin position creates a blocking stake that complicates future transaction structures.

headline: G MINING + G2 GOLDFIELDS ARRANGEMENT CLOSES — Guyana Gold Hub Created; Oko West + Oko-Ghanie Combined; G3 Goldfields Spun Out (TSX: GMIN / TSX-V: GTWO)
snippet: G Mining Ventures Corp (TSX: GMIN) announced July 29, 2026 the closing of its arrangement with G2 Goldfields, combining the Oko West gold project (the producing Tocantinzinho mine plus Oko West development) with G2's Oko-Ghanie project to create a consolidated Guyana gold platform — with identified synergies exceeding C$1 billion in combined development cost savings and shared infrastructure. Concurrent with the closing, G3 Goldfields was spun out as a separate publicly listed vehicle holding G2's legacy exploration assets outside the core Guyana package, giving G Mining shareholders optionality on early-stage discovery upside without burdening the development company. The transaction is one of the largest gold consolidation events of 2026 in the Americas and establishes Guyana — home to the first world-class gold discoveries of the current cycle — as a two-company district dominated by Goldfields (Salares Norte) and the newly enlarged G Mining.

headline: GLENCORE GOES SHOPPING FOR COPPER M&A — UK Panel 6-Month Cooling-Off With Rio Tinto Expires August; New Targets In Focus As Copper Holds Above $6.40/lb
snippet: Glencore is actively pursuing copper acquisition targets as the UK Takeover Panel's mandatory six-month cooling-off period — imposed after Glencore's approach to Rio Tinto collapsed in February 2026 — expires in August 2026, freeing the Swiss commodities giant to make formal M&A overtures once again. With copper trading above US$6.40/lb and Glencore generating record cash flows from its Collahuasi, Antapaccay, and Katanga copper assets, management has signaled it views copper consolidation as a strategic priority for H2 2026. The Takeover Panel's Rule 2.8 expiry is a defined calendar catalyst for the entire copper M&A landscape: Glencore's re-entry as a live buyer compresses implied premiums for all copper developers and mid-tiers in its acquisition perimeter, and raises the floor under P/NAV multiples for mid-cap TSX copper stocks in the sub-$5 billion enterprise value range where Glencore has historically paid 1.2–1.6x NAV on acquisitions.

headline: CATL JIANXIAWO MINE SUSPENDED — ~5% Of Global Lithium Supply Offline; Carbonate Spikes Toward CNY 85,000/t; Up 96% Year-On-Year
snippet: CATL's Jianxiawo lithium mine in Sichuan — accounting for an estimated 5% of global lithium supply — has been suspended after the company failed to extend its mining permit, driving lithium carbonate prices toward CNY 85,000 per tonne in August 2026, a two-year high and up approximately 96% year-over-year despite the broader narrative of lithium oversupply that dominated H1 2026. The permit suspension is separate from the voluntary curtailments and care-and-maintenance decisions driving Australian hard-rock restarts (like Mineral Resources' Bald Hill, already covered); this is a forced supply removal event from the world's largest battery manufacturer and lithium miner. For Western lithium developers and explorers, the CATL disruption validates the argument that the lithium cycle's recovery is not demand-driven alone — supply-side fragility in Chinese domestic production is an independent price support mechanism that has been underweighted in analyst models.

headline: NORTHERN STAR AT DIGGERS: NEW CEO VADNAGRA (FROM GLENCORE) FACES ELLIOTT'S A$1B+ STRATEGIC REVIEW PUSH — Calm Before The Storm? (ASX: NST)
snippet: Northern Star Resources (ASX: NST) presented its Diggers & Dealers 2026 investor update on August 3 in what industry commentator Dryblower characterises as the 'calm before the storm' — incoming CEO Suresh Vadnagra (recruited from Glencore, starting October 5) has not yet taken charge, leaving outgoing management to present a steady-state operational update while Elliott Management, which has accumulated an A$1 billion-plus strategic position, continues to press publicly for a strategic review. The tension is notable: Elliott's activist thesis (that Northern Star's asset base is worth substantially more under a different corporate structure or as an M&A target) will meet a new CEO with a Glencore pedigree who is far more familiar with asset-level deal-making than Northern Star's historically organic-growth-first board. For ASX gold investors, the Northern Star setup is one of the most structurally interesting corporate stories of H2 2026 — the Elliott-Vadnagra dynamic will determine whether Australia's second-largest gold producer remains independent or becomes an acquisition currency.

headline: YIELD CURVE TWIST: 30-YEAR TREASURY AT 5.275% AS MARKETS LOSE FED CONFIDENCE — Long End Pricing Fiscal Risk, Not Policy; Gold Floor Supported (Money Metals)
snippet: Money Metals Exchange published an August 2, 2026 analysis identifying a 'yield curve twist' dynamic in which the 30-year US Treasury yield has risen to 5.275% while shorter-duration yields have remained anchored — a pattern that markets historically read not as a straightforward rate-hike signal but as a loss of confidence in the Fed's ability to manage the long end of the curve. The distinction matters for gold investors: when the long end rises because of fiscal risk rather than growth expectations, gold tends to outperform rather than underperform, because the market is effectively pricing in a scenario where the Fed's credibility is constrained by the US debt burden. This is a distinct analytical angle from the August 1 '9-3 Vote / Cracks Inside the Fed' piece (which focused on internal policy disagreement); the Yield Curve Twist piece focuses on bond market autonomy and the fiscal-dominance risk that makes gold the beneficiary of both rate-hike AND rate-cut scenarios in the current environment.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER SET TO TAKE OFF — Mining Stocks 'Highly Undervalued'; Structural Supply Gap And Sovereign Demand Cited As Catalysts (GoldSeek)
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis published in the August 3, 2026 edition argues that gold and silver mining stocks remain highly undervalued relative to current spot prices — with gold equities trading at implied long-term gold of $3,200–$3,500/oz while spot holds above $4,067 — and that the conditions for a sustained re-rating are structurally in place: a multi-decade mining underinvestment cycle that has created a production supply gap, sovereign accumulation from BRICS-aligned central banks, and the absence of significant new major gold discoveries replacing depleted reserves. The analysis is distinct from Adam Hamilton's seasonal timing piece (already covered in the 12:28 batch); this piece focuses on the fundamental valuation gap rather than the technical/seasonal entry window, and argues the eventual re-rating to fair value could be the dominant sector theme of 2026-2027 as record senior producer FCF makes the discount increasingly difficult to sustain.

headline: PERPETUA RESOURCES SIGNS $1.8B DOE LOAN — US$182M/Yr REE AND ANTIMONY OUTPUT From Stibnite Gold-Antimony Mine In Idaho; Construction 2027 (Nasdaq: PPTA)
source_name: Investing News Network / Perpetua Resources Corp
snippet: Perpetua Resources Corp (Nasdaq: PPTA, TSX: PPTA) secured a conditional commitment for a US$1.8 billion loan from the US Department of Energy's Loan Programs Office in late July 2026 to advance the Stibnite Gold-Antimony Project in Idaho toward construction — a project targeting US$182 million per year in combined antimony and gold production at full throughput, positioned as the only permitted domestic US source of antimony (a US-designated critical mineral with over 90% of current global supply controlled by China and Russia). The DOE commitment follows the FAST-41 federal permitting approval received in Q1 2026 and positions Stibnite for a construction decision in H1 2027. For critical minerals investors, Perpetua represents the archetype of the US government's industrial policy response to Chinese export controls: a domestically permitted, fully financed antimony-gold mine backed by federal capital at a moment when antimony prices have more than doubled year-over-year.
